# Brainstorming frameworks and anti-patterns

Use these as thinking tools when they move the conversation forward. Never run every framework by default.

## Frameworks

| Framework | Use when | How |
| --- | --- | --- |
| How Might We | Turning a pain point into an opportunity | "How might we [outcome] for [user] without [constraint]?" Write 5 to 10 versions at the right level: not "improve onboarding" (too broad), not "add a tooltip" (a solution). |
| Jobs to be Done | Thinking from the user's goal, not features | "When [situation], I want to [motivation] so I can [outcome]." Look at functional, emotional and social jobs. Ask what the user "fired" to hire the product. |
| Opportunity solution tree | Linking an outcome to experiments | Outcome, then opportunities (from evidence), then several solutions per opportunity, then several cheap experiments per solution. |
| First principles | The team is stuck in "that is how it works" | State the assumption, break it into components, ask which are true constraints and which are conventions, rebuild from the true ones. |
| SCAMPER | Improving an existing product or process | Substitute, Combine, Adapt, Modify, Put to other use, Eliminate, Reverse. |
| Observe, Orient, Decide, Act | Fast-moving or competitive situations, or endless deliberation | Gather signals, make sense of them, choose a reversible bet, act, then observe again. Tempo beats perfection. |
| Reverse brainstorming | Stuck on how to solve something | Brainstorm how to make the problem worse, then reverse each idea. |
| Constraint removal | Incremental thinking | "What if there were no technical, budget or political limits?" Then work back to what is feasible. |
| Analogies and hat-switching | Need fresh angles | How does another industry solve this? How would a power user, a new user, an admin or a critic solve it? |

## Session rhythm

1. Frame: what, why now, what is known, constraints, desired outcome.
2. Diverge: quantity first, no judgment.
3. Provoke: challenge and extend.
4. Converge: themes, evaluation, top 2 or 3.
5. Capture: ideas, assumptions, questions, next steps, what was set aside.

## Anti-patterns to name

| Pattern | Sign | Response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Solutioning before framing | "We should build X" before the problem is defined | Ask which user problem X solves and how we know |
| Feature parity trap | "A competitor has X, so we need X" | Ask which need X serves and whether there is a better way |
| Anchoring on constraints | "We cannot because of Y" during divergence | Park feasibility until converging |
| One-idea brainstorm | The user arrives with a solution | "That is one approach. What are three others?" |
| Analysis paralysis | Long divergence, no convergence | "If you had to pick one direction now, which and why?" |
| Brainstorming instead of researching | The session circles a factual unknown | Stop and name the research needed |
